Illegal street racers

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We take a look into the fast and furious world of illegal street racing

Unique Selling Point:
We will take the audience into a world very few people have access to - the world of illegal street racing. We will be taking an unusual approach to the subject -meaning the story will focus less on the legality of this extreme pass time. The story will have a no holds barred feel to it and will be gritty and visually interesting. The story will not be an all-boys affair ; We have female racers who are well respected in the underground racing world and are just as passionate about cars.

Summary:
The story will immerse the audience into the secretive illegal racing scene. This will be a no holds barred approach to the subject, we will have details how racings routes are determined, we will get a glimpse into the painstaking and expensive exercise of modifying a car for a street race and the incredibly obsessive 'relationships' these street racers have with their cars. We will also look at the history of street racing in Joburg and South Africa as a whole. We will speak to the organizer of the illegal street race Dielo or Uncle 'D' who has been racing since he was a teenager. We will also be speaking to JP who claims his crew is the fastest in the country, he runs a more organized form of street racing, he says he doesn't consider himself "illegal" and blames MotorsportSA for not making enough facilities available to racers.
We will be interviewing Jess, a female racer who will be speaking about being an extreme minority in the world of racing. She has taken on experienced racers both on the street and the tracks and more often than not she has come up on top.
In esssence, the story will be mainly on the subculture

Press Release:


Despite scathing public criticism for what is seen as reckless behaviour in a sport that sees it regular share of death and injury, Carte Blanche visits the secretive world of illegal street racing with its unique subculture of men and women addicted to the adrenaline rush, who have obsessive relationships with cars that they painstakingly modify for maximum speed and power. Without trophies or monetary reward, they use public roads for their secretly convened night-time races and the prize of bragging rights and honour. We ask is this a sport that deserves to be formalised?

Script:


Illegal street racers


Upsound: People turn to drugs,other people turn to alcohol we’re car junkies

Upsound: You do get locked up, you do get fines,but as a racer it comes with the territory

Upsound:Its for the love of the game, its racing you know.

Upsound: Everybody who comes here comes at their own risk, we know what we doing is wrong,they know the risks

Upsoud: Some people scuba dive, some people jump out of aeroplanes, this is just what we do.

V/O Street racing has been around for decades , but in recent months it’s come under the spotlight following a gruesome high speed accident in Cape Town that shocked the country , when a man crashed his BMW into a barrier while reportedly travelling at 320 KM per hour during an illegal street race, suffering critical injuries and had both his legs amputated.Many called for a clampdown on these illegal circuits



V/O but despite the negative public sentiment this hasn’t deterred many of these street racers.

Upsound:. You know the story is when something goes wrong at an illegal car race the next morning you read in the news innocent bystander gets killed by a reckless street racer, drag racers are not reckless

V/O It’s a dangerous game and often competitors are simply looking for a thrill.
50 year old “Uncle D” organises many of these races in Johannesburg

Upsound Macfarlane :Uncle D you’re known as the race master take us through your journey in Motorsport.

Upsound : I was always passionate about racing, i raced for many years I got married’,I got kids . I did a lot of sanctioned events I marshalled all over.Street racing has been around forever we didnt invent it.I just took it upon myself to try to step in and make it safer.

V/O Races take place in the dead of the night and hundreds of people gather to watch different groups of adrenaline seekers go head to head on pre-determined public locations. As the racemaster “Uncle D” chooses where the races will take place and which race crews can go up against each other

Upsound:The hype starts early in the morning My phone rings early in the morning, people wanting to know where we’re racing, who we racing, weather permitting. I am the news channel regarding racing

Upsound: Macfarlane : How often do events happen?

Upsound Uncle D: There is street racing everyday of the week around Joburg.Its just a passion,other people turn to drugs, alcohol, we car junkies...you see every day of the week

V/O As one of a few female drivers, 25 year old Charne Lee Jones has been racing for four years and she’s earned her place as one of the most respected drivers on the circuit.

Upsound Charne : The drag racing scene is quite big,you’ve got drag racing spinning , drifting , track racing-anything you can pretty much imagine .When I am racing I forget whatever is going on in my life,whatever is going on at home or at work.Whatever stress I have it literally dissapears, its not in the back of my mind its not in the front of my mind ,for that space in time when I am racing I feel completely free



For me, I am not big on illegal racing,I would rather go to the track, but I can understand the illegal racing, at the end of the day if they take all the race track away we are still going to race regardless.

Upsound Uncle D: The problem is like I say money, the tracks have become so exorbitant with their fees, it can cost you up to three grand a day just to enter your car to race, we used to run Wesbank many years ago, for the year we ran Wesbank there was no single illegal even in Joburg,unfortunately the investors got an offer they sold the place, saddest day in motorsport and everyone went back to the street.

V/O Access is limited and within hours of each race, the dates and times are posted on restricted social media platforms. It’s up to the drivers and spectators to get themselves to these underground locations.

Link Macfarlane: right now we are in the middle of a secluded street in Johannesburg and as you can see there are modified cars of every kind and they are here to race on this public road.

VO: It’s all illegal and drivers fear being caught by police so they’ve asked us to hide their identities.

Upsound Racer Anit : You do get locked up , you do get fines, but as a racer it comes with the territory, it’s something we try to avoid.


UpsoundRacer 2 Anit : some people scuba dive, some people dive out of airplanes, this is what we do.

Upsound Racer 3: We want to see cars racing and its for the love of the game.

Upsound Macfarlane: people say places like this are for thugs or people who steal cars

Upsound Jase :for us its just the passion,this for us is like a drug, this for us is better than drinking or smoking, it thrills us and fulfills our passion.

V/O it’s an obsessive bond between man and machine, drivers spend thousands of Rands adapting their cars; installing state of the art turbo engines and nitro oxide systems just to go a second faster than their nearest rivals. [ Please change the visual of Charne on this piece : “ obsessive bond between man and machine”]

Upsound Uncle D : when I started we were racing 16000 Conquests with downdrafts – 36 downdrafts, its evolved, we have cars you can sit in the car and program it and you can map it,it depends on your pocket.


Upsound I spend ten twenty, thirty thousand on suspension, back ,interior wheels and engine. I don’t see it as wasting money for me its about doing something I like, its not an issue to spend the money. (visuals of her honda civic)

Upsound Racer 2 Anit: When you cross the line and you are ahead , nothing beats that feeling, all the hard work you put in your car, the late nights, early mornings… and the money as well

Upsound Jase Racer 1: Its very expensive

Upsound Macfarlane : So this car here, this is why people are making a noise ?

Upsound Jase : This is their fastest car, the Datsun.

Upsound Macfarlane: Unbelievable hey.

V/O But this is not only the realm of expensively modified modern cars, the undisputed champion of these streets is a rebuilt 1972 Datsun, twelve hundred affectionately nicknamed Makhulu Baas, This mechanical marvel is capable of reaching speeds of 220 KM/hr over a 400 meter distance.

Upsound Macfarlane When This car arrived the car went crazy why?

Upsound Ambrose (Datsun owner) : Man I think its because of the age, they say old cars dont die they go faster.

Upsound Ambrose : it took five years to get it to get it where it is.
basically whats in there is a standard 1600 engine, we basically played around with it

Upsound Macfarlane : Its called Makhulu Baas , why that name ?

Upsound Ambrose :We chose Makhulu baas because no one could catch us on the street.

V/O As the smell of burning rubber fills the air... it was time to race:

-Racing visuals-

V/O After a furious night of racing, it’s down to Makhulu Baas and a modified Nissan Skyline GTR … and just as predicted, the crowd favorite - Makhulu Baas takes the victory…

V/O With many saying a legal race track is not an option, street racers are calling on city officials to come up with innovative alternatives.

Upsound Racer Anit Maybe If they could open up a section of the road once a week for us for four hours a night to get it out of our systems everyone would be happy- chappy

V/O Safety marshals can be found all over the designated racing strip, but fans attending these illegal races come in their hundreds, and at these high speeds anything can happen. A single hit or a swerve could be fatal.

Upsound :Everybody that comes here comes at their own risk, they know what they wrong,ng is wrong , they know the risks , if you get told by the marshals to stand back and you don’t , you end up getting hurt

V/O They do it for nothing more than bragging rights and the thrill of the moment, and without any viable legal alternatives, street racing is here to stay because for some there is no risk too great in the quest to satisfy their need for speed.

mihle@combinedartists.co.za 09 December 2019 10 March 2019 - Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 28 June 2019 Press Release: Despite scathing public criticism for what is seen as reckless behaviour in a sport that sees it regular share of death and injury, Carte Blanche visits the secretive world of illegal street racing with its unique subculture of men and women addicted to the adrenaline rush, who have obsessive relationships with cars that they painstakingly modify for maximum speed and power. Without trophies or monetary reward, they use public roads for their secretly convened night-time races and the prize of bragging rights and honour. We ask is this a sport that deserves to be formalised? Script: Illegal street racers Upsound: People turn to drugs,other people turn to alcohol we’re car junkies Upsound: You do get locked up, you do get fines,but as a racer it comes with the territory Upsound:Its for the love of the game, its racing you know. Upsound: Everybody who comes here comes at their own risk, we know what we doing is wrong,they know the risks Upsoud: Some people scuba dive, some people jump out of aeroplanes, this is just what we do. V/O Street racing has been around for decades , but in recent months it’s come under the spotlight following a gruesome high speed accident in Cape Town that shocked the country , when a man crashed his BMW into a barrier while reportedly travelling at 320 KM per hour during an illegal street race, suffering critical injuries and had both his legs amputated.Many called for a clampdown on these illegal circuits V/O but despite the negative public sentiment this hasn’t deterred many of these street racers. Upsound:. You know the story is when something goes wrong at an illegal car race the next morning you read in the news innocent bystander gets killed by a reckless street racer, drag racers are not reckless V/O It’s a dangerous game and often competitors are simply looking for a thrill. 50 year old “Uncle D” organises many of these races in Johannesburg Upsound Macfarlane :Uncle D you’re known as the race master take us through your journey in Motorsport. Upsound : I was always passionate about racing, i raced for many years I got married’,I got kids . I did a lot of sanctioned events I marshalled all over.Street racing has been around forever we didnt invent it.I just took it upon myself to try to step in and make it safer. V/O Races take place in the dead of the night and hundreds of people gather to watch different groups of adrenaline seekers go head to head on pre-determined public locations. As the racemaster “Uncle D” chooses where the races will take place and which race crews can go up against each other Upsound:The hype starts early in the morning My phone rings early in the morning, people wanting to know where we’re racing, who we racing, weather permitting. I am the news channel regarding racing Upsound: Macfarlane : How often do events happen? Upsound Uncle D: There is street racing everyday of the week around Joburg.Its just a passion,other people turn to drugs, alcohol, we car junkies...you see every day of the week V/O As one of a few female drivers, 25 year old Charne Lee Jones has been racing for four years and she’s earned her place as one of the most respected drivers on the circuit. Upsound Charne : The drag racing scene is quite big,you’ve got drag racing spinning , drifting , track racing-anything you can pretty much imagine .When I am racing I forget whatever is going on in my life,whatever is going on at home or at work.Whatever stress I have it literally dissapears, its not in the back of my mind its not in the front of my mind ,for that space in time when I am racing I feel completely free For me, I am not big on illegal racing,I would rather go to the track, but I can understand the illegal racing, at the end of the day if they take all the race track away we are still going to race regardless. Upsound Uncle D: The problem is like I say money, the tracks have become so exorbitant with their fees, it can cost you up to three grand a day just to enter your car to race, we used to run Wesbank many years ago, for the year we ran Wesbank there was no single illegal even in Joburg,unfortunately the investors got an offer they sold the place, saddest day in motorsport and everyone went back to the street. V/O Access is limited and within hours of each race, the dates and times are posted on restricted social media platforms. It’s up to the drivers and spectators to get themselves to these underground locations. Link Macfarlane: right now we are in the middle of a secluded street in Johannesburg and as you can see there are modified cars of every kind and they are here to race on this public road. VO: It’s all illegal and drivers fear being caught by police so they’ve asked us to hide their identities. Upsound Racer Anit : You do get locked up , you do get fines, but as a racer it comes with the territory, it’s something we try to avoid. UpsoundRacer 2 Anit : some people scuba dive, some people dive out of airplanes, this is what we do. Upsound Racer 3: We want to see cars racing and its for the love of the game. Upsound Macfarlane: people say places like this are for thugs or people who steal cars Upsound Jase :for us its just the passion,this for us is like a drug, this for us is better than drinking or smoking, it thrills us and fulfills our passion. V/O it’s an obsessive bond between man and machine, drivers spend thousands of Rands adapting their cars; installing state of the art turbo engines and nitro oxide systems just to go a second faster than their nearest rivals. [ Please change the visual of Charne on this piece : “ obsessive bond between man and machine”] Upsound Uncle D : when I started we were racing 16000 Conquests with downdrafts – 36 downdrafts, its evolved, we have cars you can sit in the car and program it and you can map it,it depends on your pocket. Upsound I spend ten twenty, thirty thousand on suspension, back ,interior wheels and engine. I don’t see it as wasting money for me its about doing something I like, its not an issue to spend the money. (visuals of her honda civic) Upsound Racer 2 Anit: When you cross the line and you are ahead , nothing beats that feeling, all the hard work you put in your car, the late nights, early mornings… and the money as well Upsound Jase Racer 1: Its very expensive Upsound Macfarlane : So this car here, this is why people are making a noise ? Upsound Jase : This is their fastest car, the Datsun. Upsound Macfarlane: Unbelievable hey. V/O But this is not only the realm of expensively modified modern cars, the undisputed champion of these streets is a rebuilt 1972 Datsun, twelve hundred affectionately nicknamed Makhulu Baas, This mechanical marvel is capable of reaching speeds of 220 KM/hr over a 400 meter distance. Upsound Macfarlane When This car arrived the car went crazy why? Upsound Ambrose (Datsun owner) : Man I think its because of the age, they say old cars dont die they go faster. Upsound Ambrose : it took five years to get it to get it where it is. basically whats in there is a standard 1600 engine, we basically played around with it Upsound Macfarlane : Its called Makhulu Baas , why that name ? Upsound Ambrose :We chose Makhulu baas because no one could catch us on the street. V/O As the smell of burning rubber fills the air... it was time to race: -Racing visuals- V/O After a furious night of racing, it’s down to Makhulu Baas and a modified Nissan Skyline GTR … and just as predicted, the crowd favorite - Makhulu Baas takes the victory… V/O With many saying a legal race track is not an option, street racers are calling on city officials to come up with innovative alternatives. Upsound Racer Anit Maybe If they could open up a section of the road once a week for us for four hours a night to get it out of our systems everyone would be happy- chappy V/O Safety marshals can be found all over the designated racing strip, but fans attending these illegal races come in their hundreds, and at these high speeds anything can happen. A single hit or a swerve could be fatal. Upsound :Everybody that comes here comes at their own risk, they know what they wrong,ng is wrong , they know the risks , if you get told by the marshals to stand back and you don’t , you end up getting hurt V/O They do it for nothing more than bragging rights and the thrill of the moment, and without any viable legal alternatives, street racing is here to stay because for some there is no risk too great in the quest to satisfy their need for speed. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We take a look into the fast and furious world of illegal street racing
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We will take the audience into a world very few people have access to - the world of illegal street racing. We will be taking an unusual approach to the subject -meaning the story will focus less on the legality of this extreme pass time. The story will have a no holds barred feel to it and will be gritty and visually interesting. The story will not be an all-boys affair ; We have female racers who are well respected in the underground racing world and are just as passionate about cars.
metadata.Summary: The story will immerse the audience into the secretive illegal racing scene. This will be a no holds barred approach to the subject, we will have details how racings routes are determined, we will get a glimpse into the painstaking and expensive exercise of modifying a car for a street race and the incredibly obsessive 'relationships' these street racers have with their cars. We will also look at the history of street racing in Joburg and South Africa as a whole. We will speak to the organizer of the illegal street race Dielo or Uncle 'D' who has been racing since he was a teenager. We will also be speaking to JP who claims his crew is the fastest in the country, he runs a more organized form of street racing, he says he doesn't consider himself "illegal" and blames MotorsportSA for not making enough facilities available to racers. We will be interviewing Jess, a female racer who will be speaking about being an extreme minority in the world of racing. She has taken on experienced racers both on the street and the tracks and more often than not she has come up on top. In esssence, the story will be mainly on the subculture
